question: A chair produced by Elm Furniture yields a profit of $43, while every dresser yields a $52 profit. Each week, 17 gallons of stain and 11 lengths of oak wood are available. Each chair requires 1.4 gallons of stain and 2 lengths of oak wood, while each dresser requires 1.1 gallons of stain and 3 lengths of oak wood. Determine the maximum profit.

candidates.code:
import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "products": ["chair", "dresser"],
    "resources": ["stain", "oak"],
    "profit": {"chair": 43, "dresser": 52},
    "availability": {"stain": 17, "oak": 11},
    # usage[resource][product]
    "usage": {
        "stain": {"chair": 1.4, "dresser": 1.1},
        "oak": {"chair": 2, "dresser": 3},
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])
    model.R = pyo.Set(initialize=d["resources"])

    # x[p] = number of units of product p produced (indivisible units)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Per-resource usage lookup params
    model.profit = pyo.Param(model.P, initialize=d["profit"])
    model.avail = pyo.Param(model.R, initialize=d["availability"])

    def usage_rule(m, r, p):
        return d["usage"][r][p]

    model.usage = pyo.Param(model.R, model.P, initialize=usage_rule)

    # Resource capacity limits (one constraint per resource)
    def capacity_rule(m, r):
        return sum(m.usage[r, p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= m.avail[r]

    model.capacity_con = pyo.Constraint(model.R, rule=capacity_rule)

    # Objective: maximize weekly profit
    def profit_rule(m):
        return sum(m.profit[p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=profit_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

# ============================================================================
# Elm Furniture Product-Mix Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   produce["chair"]   : chairs produced per week     (NonNegativeIntegers)
#   produce["dresser"] : dressers produced per week   (NonNegativeIntegers)
#
# OBJECTIVE  (maximize)
#   Weekly profit = 43*produce["chair"] + 52*produce["dresser"]
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   (1) Stain usage : 1.4*produce["chair"] + 1.1*produce["dresser"] <= 17
#   (2) Oak usage   : 2.0*produce["chair"] + 3.0*produce["dresser"] <= 11
# ============================================================================

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "profit": {
        "chair": 43,
        "dresser": 52,
    },
    "usage": {
        "stain":    {"chair": 1.4, "dresser": 1.1},
        "oak_wood": {"chair": 2.0, "dresser": 3.0},
    },
    "availability": {
        "stain":    17,
        "oak_wood": 11,
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.PRODUCTS = pyo.Set(initialize=list(d["profit"].keys()))
    model.RESOURCES = pyo.Set(initialize=list(d["availability"].keys()))

    # ----- Parameters -------------------------------------------------------
    model.profit = pyo.Param(model.PRODUCTS, initialize=d["profit"])
    model.avail = pyo.Param(model.RESOURCES, initialize=d["availability"])

    def _usage_init(m, r, p):
        return d["usage"][r][p]

    model.usage = pyo.Param(
        model.RESOURCES, model.PRODUCTS, initialize=_usage_init
    )

    # ----- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    model.produce = pyo.Var(
        model.PRODUCTS,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
    )

    # ----- Objective (maximize profit) --------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.profit[p] * m.produce[p] for p in m.PRODUCTS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ----- Constraints: one capacity limit per resource ---------------------
    def capacity_rule(m, r):
        return sum(m.usage[r, p] * m.produce[p] for p in m.PRODUCTS) <= m.avail[r]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.RESOURCES, rule=capacity_rule)

    return model

"""
Elm Furniture weekly product-mix model.

Decision variables
------------------
x[p] : number of units of product p produced per week, p in P = {chair, dresser}
       domain: non-negative integers (units are indivisible)

Objective (maximise)
--------------------
total weekly profit = sum_p profit[p] * x[p]
    = 43 * x[chair] + 52 * x[dresser]        units: dollars/week

Constraints (source sentences)
-----------------------------
(C1) Sentence 3: weekly stain consumption <= 17 gallons.
       1.4 * x[chair] + 1.1 * x[dresser] <= 17
(C2) Sentence 3: weekly oak wood consumption <= 11 lengths.
       2.0 * x[chair] + 3.0 * x[dresser] <= 11
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # profitability ($ per unit produced)
    "profit": {"chair": 43.0, "dresser": 52.0},
    # availability of each resource
    "availability": {"stain": 17.0, "wood": 11.0},
    # per-unit resource usage: usage[product][resource]
    "usage": {
        "chair":   {"stain": 1.4, "wood": 2.0},
        "dresser": {"stain": 1.1, "wood": 3.0},
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = list(d["profit"].keys())
    resources = list(d["availability"].keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="elm_furniture_product_mix")

    # Index sets
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products, name="P")
    model.R = pyo.Set(initialize=resources, name="R")

    # Decision variables: non-negative integer production quantities
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: maximise total weekly profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Resource capacity constraints (one per resource)
    def capacity_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][p][r] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["availability"][r]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.R, rule=capacity_rule)

    return model
